resources.string: Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, Shift and the arrows above any keyboard

KeyPlus shows a strip of the keys a phone\'s keyboard lacks (Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt, Shift, the arrows, Home, End, Page up and Page down) above the keyboard that is open, and sends them to the field being typed in. It reads where the keyboard is on the screen and nothing else.

Berpiztu AI Keyboard: menus and colours
Moves the keyboard out of the way of the menus that open, and sees an app\'s colour for Theme › Per app

Berpiztu AI Keyboard sees only the field it types in. With this on, it also sees where a menu opens, an app\'s or a list that drops down, to move out of its way (Preferences › Also move out of the way of menus); and, with Theme › Colours › Per app, the colour just inside the field it types in, to take the app\'s colour (App\'s). It reads nothing else.
Android shows other apps\' menus only to an accessibility service: a tap turns on Berpiztu AI Keyboard: menus
The IP of the computer with ia-voice on your network, such as 192.168.1.20; port 8060 unless you write another.
On the glasses, the keys filling the box the headset gives a keyboard; off, the phone\'s keyboard, as any Android keyboard. It changes when the keyboard opens again

VS Code and other Electron apps tell their menus only when started with --force-renderer-accessibility: add it to their shortcut (Properties › Target, after Code.exe).

If the keyboard does not show or type in some windows (Task Manager, a terminal or an installer opened as administrator), they run as administrator and the keyboard does not: Windows lets a program into a window only when it runs as that window does.
Windows asks for permission each time the keyboard starts. Turned on, the keyboard starts again as administrator at once; turned off, it starts as usual from the next time

Each language\'s Spelling is on its page, opened with More options

A model on this device, chosen in the list, alone corrects this language: at each space it reads the sentence so far and mends its last word, and as . ? ! or Enter closes it, it writes it whole again mended (spelling, accents, punctuation and capitals). The words offered as a word is typed still come from the word list. The choices under it stay faded, kept as they are, until it is turned off

Autocorrect writes the correction in the text; Suggestions offers it in the toolbar, and the words starting as typed. Both come from what is chosen below: the context model, or the choices under it. Both off, nothing is written or offered
There is no context model on this device. They are put in %1$s, one to a folder.
The context model alone corrects this language: turn it off to use this.
Capital at the start of a sentence
The first letter of a sentence a capital, after . ? or ! and a space and on a new line, while Spelling is on; off until turned on, and on whatever is downloaded

Every language\'s Spelling at once, the capital at a sentence\'s start too, also with the toolbar\'s spellcheck button: off to write code, on again for a message; each language\'s choices stay as they are

When . ? or ! ends a sentence, a model on this device proposes its accents in the toolbar (cómo estás, está limpia); a tap applies them. Off until turned on, when it is downloaded once (diactag, 38 MB)
Typing ? or ! puts its pair at the sentence\'s start: qué quieres? becomes ¿qué quieres?
On Windows a sentence or a word is corrected only when the keyboard typed all of it, with no mouse or computer key since it began

When . ? or ! or Enter ends what was typed, a model on this device adds the full stops, commas, question marks and capitals it lacks, never taking away what was typed. Off until turned on, when it is downloaded once (%1$s MB)
The model is on this computer
The model could not be downloaded: %1$s

The model\'s accents are written as the sentence ends (. ? ! two spaces or Enter), a word\'s correction as the word ends, and ↶ in the toolbar takes them back; off, they are offered in the toolbar and a tap writes them

A word typed letter by letter that the dictionary does not have (kasa, helo) is corrected as it ends (a space, a sign or Enter) with the word it most likely meant (casa, hello), as Autocorrect has it, and words are offered as you type; the keyboard\'s word list and your dictionary\'s words are left as they are, and offered for a word near them. Off until turned on, when LibreOffice\'s %1$s dictionary and the language\'s word list are downloaded once (%2$s MB)

Correct words knows a few common misspellings of its own (hai: hay, ahí, ay), and offers, never writing it alone, what a word that is a word too is commonly written for (as: has, haz); this adds the 21,000 the Spanish Wikipedia corrects (aver: a ver, haber; ahi: ahí). Off until turned on, when its list is downloaded once (0.6 MB)

You turn it on yourself, in Android\'s switch for it. If Android says the setting is restricted, open the app\'s info, choose ⋮ at the top right, then Allow restricted settings, and try again.

Berpiztu AI Keyboard sees only the field it types in. With this on, it also sees where a menu opens, an app\'s or a list that drops down, to move out of its way (Preferences › Also move out of the way of menus). It reads nothing else, and takes no screenshot.
Where Android hides the switch (a headset), Wireless debugging turns it on, no computer needed.
